objectives.text: Define energy balance and say what happens when it tips either way.
Explain what BMI measures and where it misleads.
State the health risks associated with too much and too little body fat.
Describe what defines successful weight loss and what it usually involves.
Explain what a metabolic pathway is and what metabolism is for.

terms.gloss: Energy in equal to energy out. Weight is stable when it holds.
Weight over height squared. A population screening tool, not a measure of an individual's body fat.
The sum of chemical reactions in the body. Its goals are energy transfer and matter transport.
A series of enzyme steps turning a starting substrate into a product.
Where fat sits. Abdominal fat carries more risk than the same weight elsewhere.
Defined as intentionally losing at least ten percent of body weight and keeping it off.

options: Energy taken in equals energy spent
Calories are kept below two thousand
Carbohydrate is avoided in the evening
Meals are eaten at regular times
questions.why: Balance is the whole mechanism. Everything else is a strategy for achieving it.
distractorNotes: Needs vary widely between people.
Timing is not what decides the balance.
Regularity can help, but is not the mechanism.

options: A screening tool for populations
A direct measurement of body fat
An exact guide to an individual's health
A measure of how fat is distributed
questions.why: It is weight over height squared — cheap and useful across groups, but it cannot tell muscle from fat in one person.
distractorNotes: It measures neither fat nor its distribution.
It is too blunt to settle an individual case.
Distribution is assessed separately.

questions.prompt: A very muscular athlete may be classed overweight by BMI because:
options: BMI cannot distinguish muscle from fat
Athletes have denser bone than average
Athletes carry more water in the body
BMI uses height in metres, not inches
questions.why: It is a ratio of weight to height. Anything that adds weight raises it, whatever that weight is made of.
distractorNotes: A minor factor, not the explanation.
Also minor.
The unit is not the problem.

questions.prompt: As BMI rises above 25, risk increases for:
options: Heart disease, type 2 diabetes, hypertension
Osteoporosis, anaemia and scurvy
Lactose intolerance, coeliac disease and reflux
Vitamin A toxicity and iron overload
questions.why: These are the associations the chapter names. Association across a population is not a prediction about one person.
distractorNotes: Those are deficiency- and bone-related conditions.
Those are digestive conditions with other causes.
Those relate to excessive intakes.

questions.prompt: Worldwide, the number of people overweight or obese now:
options: Exceeds the number who are starving
Remains far below the number who starve
Is roughly equal to those starving
Has been falling for two decades
questions.why: The balance tipped, and it reframes undernutrition and overnutrition as two halves of one problem rather than opposites.
distractorNotes: The crossover has already happened.
It has passed equality.
It has risen, not fallen.

questions.prompt: Successful weight loss is defined as:
options: Losing ten percent and keeping it off
Losing any amount of weight in a month
Reaching a BMI below twenty-five
Losing weight without any exercise
questions.why: The definition includes maintenance. Losing weight is common; keeping it off is what the definition asks about.
distractorNotes: Speed is not what the definition measures.
A target, not the definition of success.
Most successful cases involve activity.

options: A series of enzyme steps to a product
A single reaction that releases energy
The route food travels through the gut
A store of energy held in the liver
questions.why: Substrate in, product out, through a sequence of enzyme-catalysed steps. Metabolism is the sum of all of them.
distractorNotes: Pathways are sequences, not single reactions.
That is the digestive tract, a different thing.
That describes glycogen.

questions.prompt: The two overall goals of metabolism are:
options: Energy transfer and matter transport
Digestion and the absorption of food
Storing fat and building more muscle
Removing waste and fighting infection
questions.why: Every pathway serves one or both: moving energy where it is needed, and moving materials where they belong.
distractorNotes: Those precede metabolism.
Two outcomes among many, not the goals.
Important functions, but not metabolism's aims.

options: Abdominal fat carries more risk
All fat carries identical health risk
Fat on the limbs is more dangerous
Distribution changes total body weight
questions.why: Where fat sits changes the risk it carries, which is why waist measurement adds information BMI cannot give.
distractorNotes: Location changes the risk.
The relationship runs the other way.
Distribution does not alter the total.

questions.prompt: Knowing your daily calorie need is useful, but the chapter stresses:
options: Also watching how your weight responds
That the figure is precise for everyone
That the number never changes with age
Counting only the calories from fat
questions.why: A calculated figure is an estimate. What your weight actually does over weeks is the better feedback.
distractorNotes: Estimates vary between individuals.
Needs change across the lifespan.
All energy-yielding nutrients count.

checklist: Work out your own BMI and say plainly what it does and does not tell you.
Estimate one day's energy in and energy out.
Name two things that would change your energy expenditure.
Say why waist measurement adds something BMI does not.
selfCheck: Did I avoid treating BMI as a measure of my own body fat?
Did I account for activity as well as intake?
applicationPrompts.aiPolicy: These are questions for you to answer. This app does not write any part of a submission.
